items.title: Xiaomi is pushing custom silicon hard
items.oneliner: Xiaomi claims Apple-class single-core CPU performance and 1.22 TB/s AI memory bandwidth. Device makers are becoming chip companies.

items.title: Reinforcement learning is reaching code art
items.oneliner: This team trained Qwen to paint with JavaScript sketches. RL is moving from answers into controllable creative programs.

items.title: Qwen's small model keeps overperforming
items.oneliner: Qwen3.8-27B hit 1595 on Code Arena WebDev and ranked ninth overall. Small open models keep eating premium territory.

items.title: Microsoft tools watermark local AI images
items.oneliner: MS Paint and Photos reportedly embed server-issued GUIDs into locally generated images. Local generation still is not fully local.

items.title: Inference engines are a new attack surface
items.oneliner: A parsing bug in an inference stack can become host takeover. Sandboxing the model is not enough anymore.

items.title: France's tax breach exposed state fragility
items.oneliner: Hackers exposed data on 678,000 taxpayers, with another claim covering 2 million more. Public-sector cyber debt is compounding.

items.title: Anthropic is enterprise-hardening MCP access
items.oneliner: Anthropic added IdP-managed authorization for MCP connectors. Agent tooling is finally getting enterprise-grade permission controls.

items.title: Persistent agents are getting real harnesses
items.oneliner: Headlong keeps agents running between prompts with shell access and memory. The harness is becoming the product.

items.title: SiFive shipped its first server platform
items.oneliner: SiFive's 32-core BigSky server gives RISC-V a real Ubuntu-ready box. Alternative CPU ecosystems are getting less theoretical.

items.title: Git hosting is collapsing into object storage
items.oneliner: Walgit serves Git from a single binary backed by S3 or GCS. Repo infrastructure is getting radically simpler.
